extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies (e.g., Michigan EGLE), regulated entities, legal practitioners, and public commenters/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register direct final rule approving Michigan's infrastructure SIP submission addressing CAA section 110(a)(2)(E)(ii) (State board requirements under CAA section 128) for the 2015 ozone NAAQS; includes EPA's statutory review approach, effective date/adverse-comment procedures, and public comment submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure SIP submission requirement (CAA section 110(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When EPA promulgates a new or revised NAAQS, CAA section 110(a)(1) requires States to make SIP submissions to provide for the implementation, maintenance, and enforcement of the NAAQS (commonly called an 'infrastructure SIP').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These submissions are the mechanism by which States show their air quality management programs have the structural components necessary to meet CAA requirements; this rule addresses Michigan's March 8, 2019, submission for the 2015 ozone NAAQS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure SIP must meet CAA section 110(a)(2) elements
rubrics_metrics.description: An infrastructure SIP submission must meet the various requirements of CAA section 110(a)(2), as applicable, for the relevant NAAQS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes some language in 110(a)(2) is ambiguous and applies its existing interpretive approach (including the September 13, 2013 Infrastructure SIP Guidance) in acting on infrastructure SIP submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review scope — facial compliance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: In the context of acting on infrastructure SIP submissions, EPA evaluates a State's SIP revision for facial compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, not for the State's implementation of its SIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may use other authorities to address issues concerning a State's actual implementation of rules, regulations, consent orders, etc., that comprise its SIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: State board requirement — majority represent public interest (CAA section 128(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 128(a)(1) requires that any board or body which approves permits or enforcement orders under the CAA shall have at least a majority of members who represent the public interest and do not derive any significant portion of their income from persons subject to permits and enforcement orders under the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies where a State actually has boards/bodies with authority to approve permits or enforcement orders; if a State has abolished such boards, this provision does not apply (see Michigan example).

rubrics_metrics.name: State board requirement — conflict of interest disclosure (CAA section 128(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 128(a)(2) requires that any potential conflicts of interest by members of such board or body or the head of an executive agency with similar powers be adequately disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found Michigan's inclusion of Michigan Civil Service Commission Rule 2-8.3(a)(1) in the SIP fulfills the disclosure requirement for section 128(a)(2) in this instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability rule for section 128(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 128(a)(1) does not apply in States that do not have State boards or bodies that approve permits or enforcement orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA applied this principle to Michigan because Michigan abolished its Environmental Rules Review Committee and Environmental Permit Review Commission by executive order, leaving permit approval authority with the Director of EGLE or the Director's designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval standard for SIP submissions under CAA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CAA, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the CAA and applicable Federal regulations; EPA's role is to approve State choices provided they meet CAA criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval merely recognizes that State law meets Federal requirements and does not impose additional Federal requirements beyond State law (see 42 U.S.C. 7410(k); 40 CFR 52.02(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule effective date and adverse-comment withdrawal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: This direct final rule will be effective January 20, 2026, unless EPA receives relevant adverse written comments by December 22, 2025; if adverse comments are received, EPA will publish a timely withdrawal of the direct final rule informing the public it will not take effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA published a parallel proposed rule to serve as the proposal if adverse comments are filed; if adverse comments are received, EPA will withdraw the direct final rule and address comments in a subsequent final rule based on the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted identified by the Docket ID No. (EPA-R05-OAR-2019-0215) at Regulations.gov or via email to the listed contact; follow online instructions for submitting comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For comments submitted at Regulations.gov, follow the site's instructions; once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from the docket. Contact the person identified in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for additional submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on comment content and form (CBI, multimedia, off-site locations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit CBI, Proprietary Business Information, or information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment. EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make; see EPA public comment policy link for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and potential redaction/withholding of submitted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Agencies review submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit information you consider to be confidential or proprietary because submissions may be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of provisions when adverse comments received
rubrics_metrics.description: If EPA receives adverse comment on an amendment, paragraph, or section of this rule and that provision may be severed from the remainder of the rule, EPA may adopt as final those provisions of the rule that are not the subject of an adverse comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters interested in particular provisions should note severability may allow non-controversial portions to become final even if other parts are withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on SIP approval applicability to Indian country and Tribal jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP approval is not approved to apply on any Indian reservation land or in any other area where EPA or an Indian Tribe has demonstrated that a Tribe has jurisdiction; in those areas the rule does not have Tribal implications and will not impose substantial direct costs on Tribal governments or preempt Tribal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Tribal jurisdiction exists, separate EPA/Tribal processes apply; see Executive Order 13175 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review and statutory determinations (EOs, PRA, RFA, UMRA, NTTAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action: is not a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866; is not subject to Executive Order 14192 (SIP actions exempt from EO 12866); does not impose an information collection burden under the Paperwork Reduction Act; is certified as not having significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act; does not contain unfunded mandates under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act; does not have federalism implications under Executive Order 13132; is not subject to Executive Order 13045; is not a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 13211; and is not subject to section 12(d) of the National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These determinations explain why the rule is exempt from or not subject to various additional administrative reviews and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved and disapproved CAA elements for Michigan's infrastructure SIP
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's approval entry for Section 110(a)(2) infrastructure requirements for the 2015 ozone NAAQS lists approved and disapproved CAA elements: Approved elements include 110(a)(2)(A), (B), (C), (D)(i)(II) Prong 3, (D)(ii), (E), (F), (G), (H), (J), (K), (L), and (M). Disapproved elements include 110(a)(2)(D)(i)(I) Prongs 1 and 2, and 110(a)(2)(D)(i)(II) Prong 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This table entry shows the specific sub-elements EPA found satisfied or not satisfied in Michigan's submission and is the operative record of EPA's action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedure for judicial review and limitations on reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 307(b)(1), petitions for judicial review of this action must be filed in the appropriate U.S. Court of Appeals by January 20, 2026. Filing a petition for reconsideration by the Administrator does not affect the finality of this action for purposes of judicial review nor extend the time for filing a petition, and shall not postpone effectiveness of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA encourages parties with objections to file comments in response to the parallel notice of proposed rulemaking so EPA can address comments via withdrawal and reproposal rather than immediate litigation.
